title: Let learners teach an AI peer
statement: Let learners teach an AI peer, explaining or defending a position to it, since expecting to explain to someone else produces deeper processing than studying to be tested.
example: In a 5th-grade classroom study, teaching an agent with self-regulation feedback beat both being taught by the agent and teaching it without that feedback.
detail: Notes on a proposed discussion with AI voices treat teachable agents, where the student teaches and the AI is taught, as a separate, well-evidenced mechanism: in a 5th-grade classroom study a teach-with-self-regulation-feedback condition beat both an agent-teaches-student condition and a bare teach-the-agent baseline (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/idea-02-ai-classmates-multi-agent-debate.md`, lines 25-28). The protégé-effect programme, a review of several studies, is cited for why: expecting to explain or defend a position to someone else produces deeper processing than studying to be tested (lines 28-30). The notes add that this inverts the risk of AI voices dominating, since the AI cannot out-argue a student it was designed not to out-know, and recommend trying a teachable-agent variant in at least one unit (lines 30-32 and 136).
against: "No direct evidence on whether **teachable-agent** or **expert-panel** is the better fit specifically for literary interpretation, versus the ecosystem/CS/math domains both research lines were built on." (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/idea-02-ai-classmates-multi-agent-debate.md`, lines 156-157). The classroom study is a field study in one domain (line 28), and in it the bare teach-the-agent baseline did worse than teaching with self-regulation feedback.

evidence.quote: The "protégé effect" research program (Chase, Biswas, Schwartz) is the standard citation for why: expecting to explain/defend a position to someone else produces deeper processing than studying to be tested **(review of a multi-study program)**.
a 5th-grade classroom study found a "teach-with-self-regulation-feedback" condition beat both an agent-teaches-student condition and a bare teach-the-agent baseline **(field study, one domain)**
Consider a **teachable-agent variant** for at least one unit: student explains/defends a reading to a deliberately under-informed AI peer, instead of or alongside experts challenging the student.
